The main takeaway from our work is that
iron loss is a function of the PWM in the inverter, the permanent magnet flux density, and the speed of the motor.

the iron loss of an IPMSM is mainly caused by the fundamental field, slot ripples and the harmonics of the permanent magnet magnetomotive forces at low-speed and maximum torque operation, whereas the iron loss due to the harmonics of permanent magnet magnetomotives forces is dominant at high-speed and flux-weakening operation.
the iron loss of a motor is not a constant value, but it varies depending on the driving condition and it is important to consider the variation in the design of the motor and its inverter system.
